title: Uzbekistan’s dream finish: Olympiad gold in Samarkand
summary: China’s new generation shines and Kazakhstan and India complete the Women’s medal podium. Uzbekistan won the Open section of the 2026 Chess Olympiad on home soil in Samarkand, defeating Ukraine 2.5–1.5 in the final round to claim their second Olympiad title after Chennai 2022. India took silver following a 2–2 draw with Hungary, while Germany secured bronze with a 2.5–1.5 victory over the Netherlands.  China claimed the Women’s gold medal with a convincing 3–1 victory over Vietnam in the final round, while Kazakhstan secured silver after a 2–2 draw with Poland. India took bronze on tiebreak after also drawing 2–2 with Georgia. Full results 46th Chess Olympiad Timur Turlov, elected as the eighth FIDE President yesterday, made the ceremonial first move for Nodirbek Abdusattorov, playing 1.e4, after congratulating all the players on their performances throughout the Olympiad. Turlov also shared a heartfelt handshake with Ukrainian chess legend Vasyl Ivanchuk, who was playing on board two. Rashid Talipov, Responsible Official of the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan, made the ceremonial first move for Nodirbek Yakubboev, playing on board three for the Uzbekistan team. The venue also burst into applause when the Chief Arbiter presented GM Tin Jingyao of Singapore with the Svetozar Gligoric Fair Play Prize. During Round 6 of the Almaty Qonayev Cup in 2025, Tin’s opponent arrived after the default time because of heavy traffic. Although Tin was entitled to claim a win by forfeit, he chose instead to allow his opponent to play. Open section Uzbekistan wins the Olympiad on home soil With a decisive 2.5–1.5 victory over Ukraine, Uzbekistan won the 2026 Olympiad in Samarkand, claiming the title on home soil. Although a 2–2 draw would probably have been enough to secure gold, reserve board Mukhiddin Madaminov delivered the decisive point on board four, finishing the event with an outstanding unbeaten score of 5.5/7. His performance fully justified his selection for the team. The other three games ended in draws; Nodirbek Abdusattorov pressed hard in a bishop ending with an extra pawn, but let the win slip away at the very end. This is Uzbekistan’s second Olympiad victory, following their triumph in Chennai in 2022, with four of the five players from that team repeating their success in Samarkand. Abdusattorov also takes home the individual gold medal for board one, recording an outstanding 2869 performance rating. India takes silver, Germany claims bronze India secured the silver medal after a 2–2 draw with Hungary. Arjun Erigaisi overcame Peter Leko with Black on board two, while Gleb Dudin produced the result of his tournament by defeating World Champion Gukesh D on board four. Dudin’s victory secured him the individual gold medal on first reserve board, while Gukesh finished with the silver medal on board four. Germany claimed bronze after defeating the Netherlands 2.5–1.5, with Matthias Bluebaum scoring the decisive win against Jorden van Foreest on board two. Frederik Svane took the individual gold medal on board three with an impressive 2796 performance rating. All three medal-winning teams had occupied the top boards throughout much of the tournament, making their final positions a reflection of their consistent performances across the eleven rounds. The United States, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Hungary shared fourth to seventh place, while China dropped to eighth after spending much of the tournament among the leaders. Wei Yi nevertheless secured the individual gold medal on board two. Women’s Section China claims Women’s gold in style China dominated Vietnam 3–1 in the final match to clinch the gold medal in convincing fashion. On board one, Zhu Jiner led the team’s triumph with a win against Le Thao Nguyen Pham, finishing the Olympiad with an outstanding unbeaten score of 7/9. She also secured the individual gold medal on board one, capping an excellent tournament. Charlize van Zyl interviewed Zhu in the media area immediately after the game. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=chknoIwZLGM Although China’s women’s team also boasts such world-class players as Hou Yifan, World Champion Ju Wenjun, Lei Tingjie and Tan Zhongyi, their performance in Uzbekistan has shown that the country’s next generation of elite players is more than capable of delivering at the highest level, even in the absence of its highest-rated stars. China’s other win came on board three, where Lu Miaoyi (pictured below, center) continued her remarkable tournament with a decisive victory over Phuong Hanh Luong. The 16-year-old remained unbeaten throughout the Olympiad, scoring an impressive 9.5/11. Her performance underlines the strength and depth of Chinese women’s chess, and suggests that many more medals could be on the horizon for the young star. Lu also took home the individual gold medal on board three. Kazakhstan takes silver as India secures bronze Kazakhstan, who spent much of the Olympiad fighting on the top boards, secured the silver medal after drawing 2–2 with Poland in the final round. Aleksandra Maltsevskaya defeated Alua Nurman on board two, but Elnaz Kaliakhmet levelled the match for Kazakhstan with a win over Alicja Sliwicka on board four. The victory also secured Kaliakhmet the individual gold medal on board four. India, the United States, Poland, Armenia and Mongolia all finished on the same match-point total, but India claimed the bronze medal on tiebreak after drawing 2–2 with Georgia in the final round. Alice Lee of the United States took the individual gold medal on board two with a performance rating of 2572, while India’s Shri B Savitha secured the board-five gold medal. Humpy finds a stunning tactical finish against Dzagnidze Position of the day Humpy Koneru – Nana Dzagnidze Nana Dzagnidze, Georgia’s first board, had just played 18…Rfd8, opening the f8-square as an escape route for her king while putting additional pressure on the d4-pawn. Humpy Koneru was tactically alert, however, and responded with a wonderful combination beginning with 19.Nf6+!, sacrificing the knight. After 19…gxf6, which was forced, Humpy continued with 20.Qxh6, creating multiple threats against the black king, including Rg3 or Bh7+ followed by mate in three. title: Fireworks, drones and champions: Samarkand’s grand Olympiad finale
summary: What an amazing way to finish the Olympiad! The Uzbekistan Local Organising Committee put on a show for the ages – one of the best closing ceremonies I have attended, and I have been to many! Category prizes At around 7PM, the celebrations kicked off with the category prizes, with medals awarded to the best teams in five different rating categories, A to E, in both the Open and Women’s sections. Chief Arbiters Ivan Syrovy and Laurent Freyd announced the awardees, who were then presented with their medals by official representatives. The United States of America (A), Vietnam (B), Ecuador (C), Pakistan (D) and Qatar (E) were the five winning teams in the Open section. In the Women’s section, the gold medallists were the United States of America (A), Croatia (B), Sri Lanka (C), Ghana (D) and Maldives (E). But this was only the beginning. The prize-giving quickly gave way to an evening of music, colour, dance and spectacle, as the organisers transformed the closing ceremony into a celebration worthy of two weeks of extraordinary chess in Samarkand. Best uniforms Then it was time for another much-anticipated part of the evening: the prizes for the best uniforms. With teams having brought an impressive array of colours, styles and national flair to Samarkand, the awards recognised the most striking outfits in three categories – classic, sports and original – across the Open and Women’s sections. Hong Kong, Jamaica, South Africa, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Mali and, once again, South Africa took home the honours across the different categories and sections. From elegant and traditional to sporty and downright eye-catching, the teams certainly proved that there is more than one way to make an impression at a Chess Olympiad. Individual board medals Immediately afterwards, the spotlight turned to the individual board medals, recognising the players who had produced the strongest performances on each of the five boards over the course of the Olympiad. In the Open section, gold went to GM Nodirbek Abdusattorov on board one, GM Wei Yi on board two, GM Frederik Svane on board three, GM Ihor Samunenkov on board four and GM Gleb Dudin on the reserve board. The Women’s section had its own stellar line-up of board winners: GM Zhu Jiner took gold on board one, IM Alice Lee on board two, IM Lu Miaoyi on board three, WIM Elnaz Kaliakhmet on board four and IM Savitha Shri B  on the reserve board. The full list of individual and team medals and awards can be consulted here Music, dance and opera In between the awards, the 2,000-plus guests were treated to a succession of live music, traditional dance and opera performances, adding a distinctly Uzbek flavour to the celebrations. The magnificent Amphitheatre of the Eternal City, set along Samarkand’s Silk Road, provided a spectacular backdrop. The main awards Around 8:30PM, the moment everyone had been waiting for finally arrived: the main awards. With the closing ceremony now in full swing, the stage welcomed a host of distinguished dignitaries, including Timur Turlov, Viswanathan Anand and Mahir Mamedov, who joined the medal presentations. First up were the champions of the Women’s Section. China received the gold medals and the Vera Menchik Cup, with Kazakhstan taking silver and India bronze. As the Chinese team proudly stood on stage with the trophy, the national anthem of China rang out across the amphitheater. Then came the grand finale of the Open section. Uzbekistan, the hosts, were crowned Olympiad champions, receiving the gold medals and the Hamilton Russell Cup. India took silver, while Germany claimed bronze. The celebrations reached another emotional high as the national anthem of Uzbekistan was played to a huge reception from the home crowd. And there was still one final trophy to be presented. The Gaprindashvili Cup, awarded to the federation with the best combined result in the Open and Women’s sections, went to India – adding another major prize to an already highly successful Olympiad for the Indian team. Passing the Olympiad flag As tradition dictates, the closing ceremony then turned its attention to the future. The Olympiad flag was formally handed over to the hosts of the next edition to be held in the UAE in 2028. Hussein Abdullah Al-Khoury, the Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Chess Club and the Tournament Director of the 47th Chess Olympiad and Abdulraheem Al Zarooni, Corporate Communications Office Director – Abu Dhabi Sports Council, Chairman of the Accomodation and Travel Committee for 47th FIDE Chess Olympiad in UAE, received the flag from Alisher Sadullayev, First Vice President of the Uzbekistan Chess Federation. As the handover took place on stage, the giant screens came alive with images of Abu Dhabi, offering the thousands of guests a first glimpse of the city that will welcome the chess world for the next Olympiad in 2028. A spectacular farewell To bring the ceremony to its conclusion, FIDE President Timur Turlov took to the stage to thank President Shavkat Mirziyoyev for his tremendous support for chess and for the Olympiad. He also expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov, as well as to the governments, chess federations and organising committees whose work had made the event possible. After a few more words of encouragement, translated into Uzbek for the local audience, Turlov received a warm round of applause before officially declaring the 46th Chess Olympiad closed. And then, fittingly, the sky became the final stage of the evening. Magnificent fireworks burst over Samarkand, accompanied by a spectacular drone light show that illuminated the night sky above the Eternal City. It was a memorable farewell to the thousands of players, captains, officials and delegations who will soon return home, carrying with them not only the memories of two weeks of extraordinary chess, but also a taste of Uzbekistan, Samarkand and the legendary Silk Road.
